question.leadin: This leader was assassinated by Nathuram Godse [God-say] in 1948.
question.text: Name this central figure of India's independence movement who was given the honorific "Mahatma," or "Great Soul."
question.clue: With Lord Irwin, this person ended the salt tax in exchange for ending the Salt March.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Din-i Ilahi.
swap.text: The Din-i Ilahi was a new syncretic religion promulgated by Akbar, the ruler of this empire. This Muslim empire ruled over most of India under its last major emperor, Aurangzeb.
swap.clue: The "Nine Jewels" were employed by a monarch of this empire who abolished a tax on non-Muslims.

question.text: Rajendra Chola also defeated this island's kingdom of Anuradhapura. Arab merchants monopolized this island's city of Colombo to trade with its Sinhalese kingdoms.
question.answerHtml: Sri Lanka [or Ceylon; or the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka; or Ilangai Jananayaka Socialisa Kudiarasu; or Sri Lanka Prajatantrika Samajavadi Janarajaya]
question.clue: The JVP communist party in this country launched a daring 1989 raid on a temple housing a tooth relic.

swap.leadin: It was built by the Jamuna River by Shah Jahan for his third wife.
swap.text: Name this white marble mausoleum with a prominent dome in Agra, India.
swap.clue: This building's mausoleum has a reverberation time of 28 seconds, so that prayers conducted by the hafiz from the Quran would linger as long as possible.

question.leadin: After Sambhaji, the founder of the Maratha Empire, refused to convert to Islam, this ruler brutally executed him.
question.text: Name this emperor who reinstated the jizya tax on non-muslims, the successor to his father Shah Jahan.
question.clue: This ruler was denounced in an "epistle of victory," or Zafarnama, written by Gobind Singh.

swap.text: This foreign leader ordered the RAW ["R-A-W"] to help train and arm Bangladeshi insurgents. The assassination of this Indian leader led to the launch of Operation Blue Star.
swap.clue: This leader ordered air strikes in response to Operation Chingiz Khan to support a "Liberation War" against a 1971 genocide launched by Operation Searchlight.

question.leadin: Answer the following about national leaders following successful independence movements.
question.text: Tajuddin Ahmad served as this nation's first Prime Minister after rising to power through his party, the Awami League. It broke away from Pakistan in 1971 to form a new nation with capital Dhaka.
question.clue: A terrorist attack in this country saw five hundred small bombs explode at various government buildings within a span of 30 minutes; that attack was carried out by the JMB.

swap.text: This ruler hid with his son in baskets designated for sweets to escape the clutches of Aurangzeb. More famously, he ripped open the stomach of Afhal Khan after he tried to murder him. This man is known for establishing the Maratha Empire.
swap.clue: That general, Afzal Khan, was the subordinate of Sultan Ali Adil Shah of the Bijapur region, where this man engaged in guerrilla warfare.

question.text: The idea of partition was championed by Muhammad Iqbal and other members of this religious association within British India that was eventually led by Jinnah.
question.clue: Thousands of deaths followed this party's call for a general strike on Direct Action Day.

swap.text: Facing an uprising by his Muslim subjects, Maharaja Hari Singh, who ruled a princely state named for this region and Jammu, decided to join India. The Kargil War was among the many wars fought over this region.
swap.clue: The Poonch Rebellion preceded the signing of this region's Instrument of Accession by Hari Singh.

question.leadin: These writings were called "inscriptions of the dharma" by their creator.
question.text: Name these writings, often inscribed on either pillars or rocks, and whose instances were accompanied by the planting of banyan trees and mango groves.
question.clue: These documents outline a policy of proselytism towards the neighboring king Antiochus I, though they promote tolerance of all religions.

swap.text: This soldier led the British forces at Plassey. He had earlier successfully taken and held Arcot through a siege by Chanda Sahib, an action that caused Pitt the Elder to describe him as the "heaven-born general."
swap.clue: The definitive biography of this man is H.H. Dodwell's, which contrasts him to his French counterpart, Joseph Dupleix.

question.text: The day after the mosque's invasion, protesters burned down this city's U.S. embassy. It replaced Karachi as Pakistan's capital in 1961.
question.clue: Built in 1960, name this city that became the capital of a South Asian nation that split from India in 1947.

swap.leadin: Kenya's oldest print newspaper was founded by an immigrant from this colony.
swap.text: Give this colony. Immigrants from this colony formed an ambulance corps that helped save lives at the Battle of Spion Kop during the Boer War.
swap.clue: Lord Curzon established this colony's North-West Frontier Province, whose western border was set at the Durand Line to settle the Great Game with Russia.

question.leadin: The lead up to this agreement saw Mohandas Gandhi imprisoned at the Yerwada Central Jail.
question.text: Name this agreement wherein Gandhi negotiated a unified Hindu electorate, as opposed to the Communal Award that had been supported by Ramsay Macdonald and Bhimrao Ambedkar.

swap.leadin: Name these Muslim polities with historical caste systems.
swap.text: The Muslim conquerors who established this sultanate in the 13th century referred to themselves as ashraf, or sons of Muhammad, and eventually split into groups loosely aligned with the local caste system. The last line of rulers of this state came from the Lodi dynasty.
swap.clue: This polity's ruling dynasties included the Burji and Khilji, and rulers of this polity including Balban were former slave soldiers known as ghulams.

question.leadin: Name these events from the reign of England's George II FTPE.
question.text: This great battle would give the British control of Bengal and make Robert Clive the founder of their vast empire in India.
question.clue: It took place a year after the death of the beloved Alivardi Khan, whose nephew was killed by the son of the perfidious Mir Jafar following it.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about violent events in the lead-up to Indian independence.
swap.text: A spate of politically-motivated assassinations followed after Lord Curzon announced this 1905 territory-changing action, which was more limited in scope than a similar 1947 action accompanying Indian independence.
swap.answerHtml: Partition of Bengal [accept synonyms, accept descriptive equivalents, like the creation of West and East Bengal]

question.text: The death of Queen Tripurasundari and the adulthood of a king of this name led to Bhimsen Thapa's fall from power and suicide. A king of this name succeeded his father Raja Raja as second king of the Chola kingdom.
question.clue: A ruler with this regnal name, his empire's last, died in Pazhayarai in 1279 after submitting to Jatavarman Sundara.

swap.text: This successor of Rajaraja I conquered the Srivijaya kingdom, the Pegu islands, and managed to extract credit from Khmer.
